key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier neural operator reconstructs unsteady 3D floating-wind-turbine wakes from two observation planes and transfers learned wake dynamics across turbine scales.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support downstream-inflow assessment in floating wind farms with limited wake measurements.
method: Generate fixed and surge–pitch wake data using large-eddy simulation coupled with an actuator line model.
Combine 4D spectral convolutions with incompressible continuity and rotor-forced momentum-residual regularization.
Train on 5 MW turbine cases and transfer-learn to a 22 MW turbine.
evidence_signal: In simulation-based tests, 10% planar sampling nearly matched dense-sampling accuracy (relative L2 error 0.0689 versus 0.0684), while transfer learning reduced 22 MW streamwise-velocity error at St = 0.6 by 36% versus zero-shot inference.
watch_item: Fine-scale vortex breakdown remains damped, and the reported results establish performance on simulated rather than field-measured wakes.
paper_title: Three-Dimensional Wake Reconstruction and Cross-Scale Transfer for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines via Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operators
